newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy cabinet wins confidence vote in Senate.
newsitem.headline: Italy cabinet wins confidence vote in Senate.

text.p: Italy's government won a confidence vote in the Senate on Saturday to sweep aside opposition amendments blocking passage of a bill on the funding of public works projects for millennium celebrations in Rome.
The cabinet won the vote, the latest of several confidence votes the government has used to push bills through parliament, by 150 votes to 67.

Environment Minister Edo Ronchi called the vote earlier on Saturday, saying the government could not address numerous amendments presented by the secessionist Northern League party as the bill needed to be approved before a deadline on Sunday.

The bill, which was approved by the lower house Chamber of Deputies on Friday, allocates 3.5 trillion lire ($2.3 billion) for public works projects to prepare the Italian capital for the end-of-the-century celebrations.
The city of Rome and the Vatican are gearing up for an influx of some 20 million visitors in the year 2000, which Pope John Paul has declared a holy year, or jubilee.

"The government is committed to doing all it can to get the country ready for an extraordinarily important event...which will bring millions of pilgrims to Italy," Antonio Bargone, deputy public works minister, told the Senate.
